meaning: to be cool; to be refreshing
to be clear (sky); to be clean (water)
to be cloudy; to be overcast
to be fun; to be interesting
to get up; to wake up
to get off; to come down
to not exist; to not have
to transfer (to another bus or train)
to be many; to be a lot
to be few; to be little
to be high; to be tall (buildings)
to be wide; to be spacious
to be narrow; to be cramped
to be cool; to be stylish
to be okay; to be fine
to be kind; to be friendly
to be needed; to be necessary
to be unpleasant; to not want
not really; not particularly (with a negative)
that (+ noun, near you or already mentioned)
Nice to meet you. (first meeting, very polite)
Thank you for the meal. (before eating)
Thank you for the meal. (after eating)
I don't know. / I'm not sure.
Thank you for your hard work.
thing; fact; the one (colloquial form of 것)
note: Bound noun: it follows a modifier (먹을 거, 큰 거). 거예요 = 것이에요, 거야 is casual. Spoken contraction of 것.

meaning: thing; the one (standard form; 거 in speech)
note: Bound noun used after a modifier: 먹을 것 (something to eat), -을 것이다 (will). Before a vowel it links: 것이 → [거시]; 것은 → [거슨].

meaning: you (to a close friend or younger person)
note: Informal 'you', only for close friends or juniors. With the subject marker it becomes 네가 (written/spoken 니가). Avoid with elders.

meaning: to be so; to be like that
note: ㅎ-irregular: 그래요, 그런, 그렇게. Common: 그렇군요, 그렇지요.

meaning: you (between spouses or in arguments); darling
note: Not used for polite address to strangers (can sound rude). Used between married couples, in songs and in fights. Also can mean a respectful 'oneself' for elders (당신의 몸).
Same word as the auxiliary; always follows -지. Short form is 안 + verb.
Bound noun used in -ㄹ 수 있다/없다 (can / cannot; there is a way). Always follows a modifier.

meaning: to be how; to be what kind of
note: ㅎ-irregular: 어때요? 어떻게, 어떤. Usually appears in conjugated forms like 어때요.
Casual reply of agreement or surprise (그래?). Polite form: 그래요. Contracted from 그러다/그렇다.
Native Korean number 하나 becomes 한 before counters: 한 명, 한 개. Can also mean 'about' (한 시간쯤) or 'same' (한 반).
Contraction of 그것. Refers to something near the listener or already mentioned. Also 그게 = 그것이, 그건 = 그것은.

meaning: to quit; to stop; to leave undone
note: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ: 마세요, 맙시다. Mostly seen in -지 말다 (don't) and -다 말다 (stop halfway). Synonym of 그만두다 in some uses.
Contraction of 이것. 이게 = 이것이, 이건 = 이것은. Used for something near the speaker.
Used as -고 싶다 = 'want to do'. For first/second person; third person: -고 싶어 하다. Pronounced [십따].
Used after a modifier: 어릴 때 (when young), 갈 때 (when going). Not a precise clock time (use 시간).

meaning: just (for no reason; as it is)
note: Very common in speech: 그냥 갈래요 (I'll just go), 그냥요 (no reason).

meaning: to do so; to act like that
note: Contraction of 그리하다. Common forms: 그러면 (then), 그러니까 (so), 그러나 (but), 왜 그래요? (what's wrong?).
Expresses realization, surprise or sudden feeling; tone changes the nuance.
Used for people, animals and plants. Polite/honorific: 돌아가시다. Also exaggeration: 배고파 죽겠다.

meaning: to be correct; to be right
note: Answer is right: 답이 맞다. Also 맞아요 = 'that's right'.
Takes an object: 손님을 맞다. Also used for new year, season: 새해를 맞다.

meaning: to be hit; to get beaten
note: Also 비를 맞다 (get rained on), 주사를 맞다 (get an injection).
Casual 'no' (polite: 아니요). Also used to start a reply or show surprise: 아니, 이게 뭐야?
Comes before a noun: 그런 사람. From 그렇다 (to be like that).

meaning: to be seen; to be visible
note: Passive of 보다: 산이 보여요. Also 'to seem' with 처럼/아/어 보이다.
Causative of 보다: 친구에게 사진을 보이다. 보여 주다 is more common in speech.
고마워요 (polite), 고맙습니다 (formal). Casual: 고마워. ㅂ-irregular.

meaning: to do for the sake of; to care for
note: Mostly used as 을/를 위해(서) 'for ...' : 너를 위해 만들었어. Also 위한 + noun.
Mostly used in writing; in speech people use 그 사람 or the name. Counterpart: 그.
Comes before a noun: 다른 사람 (another person). From 다르다 (to be different).

meaning: to face; to treat; to deal with
note: Common patterns: ~에 대해(서) 'about', ~에 대한 + noun, 사람을 대하다 'treat people'.
Comes before a noun: 모든 사람 (everyone).
Before a noun: 이런 음식. Also as an exclamation: 이런! (Oh no!).
Common verb: 생각하다 (to think), 생각이 나다 (to come to mind).

meaning: you (used to a younger or lower-status person)
note: Used by older people or superiors to adults of lower standing, usually men. Do not use to elders.
Bound noun after time words: 일 년 전 (a year ago), 식사 전 (before a meal).
Causative of 죽다: 굶겨 죽이다. It is a strong word; also used in slang like 죽여준다.

meaning: during; in the middle of; among (bound noun)
note: Attaches to a noun: 회의 중 (in a meeting), 공사 중 (under construction), 이 중에서 (among these).
Contraction of 아이. 애가 = child (subject). Can also mean 'this kid/person' in casual talk.

meaning: way or method of doing something (bound noun)
note: Used as -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다 = to know/not know how to do. Also: -(으)ㄴ 줄 알았다 = thought that (but wrong).
Also means a queue or row: 줄을 서다 (to line up), 줄을 긋다 (to draw a line).
Bound noun, informal and often rude for a man (나쁜 놈). Can be affectionate among close friends. Avoid with strangers or elders.
Contraction of 이야기, very common in speech: 얘기하다 = to talk.
Used as N 때문에 (because of N) or V-기 때문에 (because). Also N 때문이다 = it is because of N.

meaning: to occur; to come out; to arise (e.g. smell, fever)
note: Used with many nouns: 열이 나다 (have a fever), 소리가 나다 (a sound is made), 생각이 나다 (come to mind). Also an auxiliary after -고 (끝나다 type compounds).
Casual contraction of 아니야. Used in 반말 to deny something. Polite: 아니에요.
Used as 짐을 지다 or 가방을 등에 지다 (carry a load on the back). Also figuratively: 책임을 지다 (take responsibility).

meaning: to set (of the sun or moon); to fade
note: 해가 지다 = the sun sets. Also used for flowers falling: 꽃이 지다.
Used with 에: 전쟁에 지다, 경기에 지다. Opposite: 이기다 (to win).

meaning: to want; to wish for; to desire
note: More formal than 바라다/싶다. Takes an object: 원하는 것 (what you want). Pronounced normally; ㅎ between sonorants may weaken in speech.
Casual 'yes' for friends or younger people. Use 네 with elders or in polite speech.
Pattern: N을/를 믿다. 믿어요 is pronounced 미더요 (linking).

meaning: to be like this; to be so
note: ㅎ-irregular: 이래요, 이런 (such), 이렇게 (like this). Related: 그렇다, 저렇다.
미안해 (casual), 미안해요 (polite), 미안합니다 (formal). For deeper apology use 죄송합니다.
Also a noun: 잠깐만요 = just a moment, please. 잠깐 기다리세요 = please wait a moment.
Native Korean number form used before counters: 두 개, 두 명, 두 시. Standalone form is 둘.
Used to urge someone: 어서 오세요 (welcome), 어서 드세요 (please eat). Similar to 빨리 but also invites.

meaning: place; case; circumstance (bound noun, e.g. 가는 데)
note: Bound noun that always follows a modifier: 아픈 데 (a place that hurts), 가는 데 (in going). Also contracted from 곳 in speech.

meaning: oh; uh; huh (exclamation of surprise or hesitation)
note: Also casual 'yes' to a friend or junior (반말). Not used to superiors.
Before a vowel-initial particle the ㅅ links: 곳이 → 고시. Casual speech often uses 데.
Reflexive 'oneself' (자기 자신), and also an affectionate 'honey' between couples.
Common in 그만하다 / 그만 먹다 (stop doing). 그만 + verb means 'stop'; also means 'unintentionally' in some uses.
Also 'talk/nonsense' as in 무슨 소리야? (What are you talking about?).

meaning: to give (humble form of 주다); to offer
note: Humble verb. 인사를 드리다 = to greet respectfully; also used as 말씀드리다 and with -아/어 드리다 (do for someone).
Used for strong pleading: 제발 도와주세요. Stronger than 좀.
Used for time (바로 가다 = go right away), direction (straight) and emphasis (바로 여기 = right here).

meaning: come on; here; now then (to draw attention)
note: Used to urge action or hand something over: 자, 시작합시다.
Also a noun: 계속되다 (to continue), 계속하다 (to continue doing). Pronounced 게속 is allowed.

meaning: to catch; to hold; to grab
note: Also used for 택시를 잡다 (catch a taxi), 약속을 잡다 (set an appointment).

meaning: but; by the way (contraction of 그런데)
note: Spoken contraction of 그런데; avoid in formal writing.
As an auxiliary after -아/어 it shows completion or regret: 먹어 버렸어요 (ate it up).
Usually said 선생님 (honorific) to address a teacher. Plain 선생 is used for referring to or as a title (김 선생).
Spoken short form of 아니요; polite but conversational.
Plural of 너; not for superiors. The 희 is ㅢ-like only in 의, so 희 is pronounced as written; 너희 is simply 너히.
Used in questions (얼마나 걸려요?) and exclamations (얼마나 예쁜지 몰라요).
Bound noun after -(으)ㄴ/-던: 어렸을 적 (when I was young), 본 적이 있다 (have seen). Not to be confused with 敵.
Hanja 敵. With vowel particle: 적이 → 저기.
Used for a sick or injured person receiving medical care.
Common pattern: 필요하다 (to be necessary), N이/가 필요하다 (need N).

meaning: to talk, to chat (casual synonym of 이야기하다)
note: Contracted form of 이야기하다; common in speech.
Used at the start of a conditional clause, often with -(으)면: 만약 비가 오면... Also used as an adverb.
Bound noun. Attaches to a noun as a particle-like word (너뿐이다) or follows a modifier (-ㄹ 뿐이다, -ㄹ 뿐만 아니라). Written without a space after a noun, with a space after a modifier.
Takes the place being left as the object: 서울을 떠나다.

meaning: to put, to place, to leave (something somewhere)
note: Also used as an auxiliary: -아/어 두다 (do in advance and leave as is).
Often implies something foolish or bad: 바보 같은 짓. Before a vowel particle it is pronounced 지시.

meaning: to help (in general; 도와주다 for helping someone)
note: ㅂ-irregular: 도와요, 도왔어요. Synonym 도와주다 is more common in speech.
Filler used when thinking or hesitating; can also express agreement or consideration.

meaning: any, anyone, anything (no one/nothing with a negative)
note: Patterns: 아무도 (no one, with negative), 아무것도 (nothing), 아무나 (anyone at all).
Commonly 죄송합니다 / 죄송해요; more polite than 미안하다.

meaning: to pay; to put out; to submit
note: Sense hint 길을 내다 (to make a road). Very common with other nouns: 소리를 내다, 돈을 내다 (pay), 화를 내다 (get angry).

meaning: more than, over, or above (a number or level)
note: Hanja 以上. Attaches to numbers: 18세 이상. Opposite: 이하 (or less).
Hanja 異常. Often 이상하다 (to be strange) or 이상이 있다 (something is wrong).
Bound noun used after a modifier: -ㄹ 터이다 (be going to, expect), -ㄴ 터라 (since the situation is). Different from the noun 터 (site, lot).

meaning: to be well, to be at peace
note: Used mostly in greetings: 안녕하세요?, 안녕하십니까?. Asks if someone is well.
Common pattern: 수술을 받다 (to have surgery), 수술하다 (to operate).

meaning: to remain, to be left over
note: Intransitive: 음식이 남다 (food is left). The causative is 남기다 (to leave something).
Pattern: V-는 방법 (the way to do V).

meaning: to go in; to cost; to stay (at)
note: 마음에 들다 = to like (literally: to enter one's heart).

meaning: to hold, to carry (in the hand)
note: Sense: 꽃을 들다 (to hold flowers). ㄹ-irregular: 드는, 듭니다, 드세요.
감사합니다 is the polite 'thank you'. Also used as a verb: 도움에 감사하다 (to thank for help).
Exclamation of surprise or admiration: 와, 대단하다! Not the particle 와 (and/with).
Follows a time expression: 3년 동안 (for 3 years), 방학 동안 (during vacation).
Connects a reason to a result. Also used in speech to restate a point: 그러니까 내 말은…
Pattern: 이유가 있다/없다; V-는 이유 (the reason for V-ing). Often used with 때문에.
Sense 自身: 자기 자신 (oneself), 자신의 생각 (one's own thoughts).
Sense 自信: 자신이 있다/없다 (to be/not be confident), 자신감 is a close synonym.

meaning: to come into being, to occur; to get (e.g. a boyfriend)
note: Subject marked with 이/가: 문제가 생기다 (a problem arises), 남자친구가 생기다. Also 'to look (a certain way)': 잘생기다.
Usually with a negative: 아무것도 없다 (there is nothing). Often contracted to 아무거.
Polite answer, similar to 네. Often pronounced as 네 in speech. Another meaning of 예 is 'example' (例).
Pattern: 식사 후 (after a meal), V-ㄴ 후에 (after V-ing), 3일 후 (3 days later).
Common: 마음에 들다 (to like, be to one's liking), 마음이 아프다 (to be heartbroken).

meaning: right away, immediately; at the moment
note: Often used as an adverb without a particle: 당장 가자 (let's go right now). Also 당장은 (for now).
Used with close friends or people younger than you to get attention, or to show surprise. Rude to use with elders or strangers.
Praises people, clothes, or things: 멋진 사람 (a cool person). Related: 멋있다.

meaning: to reach, to extend to (influence, effect)
note: Often used as 영향을 미치다 (to affect, to have an influence on). Formal in tone.

meaning: to go crazy, to go mad
note: Also used loosely, e.g. 미칠 것 같다 (I'm going crazy). Calling someone 미쳤어? is rude.

meaning: oh my goodness, good heavens (exclamation of surprise)
note: Said when surprised, shocked or amazed. Literally 'in the world'.

meaning: to do like this, to act this way
note: Contraction of 이리하다. Common in 이러다가 (at this rate) and 이러지 마세요 (please don't do this).
Used for a completed state or action; 벌써 is more about surprise at earliness.
Used after a number or noun to mean 'about', e.g. 10분 정도 (about 10 minutes).
Contraction of 이 아이. Also used to call a child or friend: 얘, 이리 와. Subject form is 얘가.
Also used as a noun: 전부 다 (all of it). Similar to 모두.

meaning: to have, to hold (short form of 가지다)
note: Contraction of 가지다. Used before consonants (갖고, 갖는); before vowels 가지다 forms are used (가져요).
Usually used with a negative: 절대 안 돼요 (absolutely not). Also noun 'absolute'.
Used for the world people live in, e.g. 세상을 살다. Different from 세계, 'the world' as a global entity.
Bound noun attached after a full name or first name, e.g. 민수 씨. Not used for superiors.
Used to emphasize adjectives, e.g. 참 좋다. Also an interjection when remembering something: 참!
사실은 or 사실 means 'actually, in fact'.
Verb form is 사랑하다 (to love).
Common: 기분이 좋다/나쁘다 (to be in a good/bad mood).
Used in 신이 나다 (to get excited, to be in high spirits). Also means 'god' or 'shoes' (in 신발) in other senses.
Examples: 가방 속 (inside the bag), 속이 안 좋다 (stomach feels bad). Also means 'one's heart/mind'.

meaning: to do what, to happen to; how come
note: Contraction of 어찌하다. Common forms: 어쩌다가 (by chance, how come), 어쩌지? (what should I do?), 어쩔 수 없다 (cannot help it).
Often used in compounds like 총소리 (gunshot); 총을 쏘다 means to fire a gun.
Common patterns: 도움이 되다 (to be helpful), 도움을 받다/주다 (to receive/give help).

meaning: to be hard, to be tiring
note: Used for both physical and mental difficulty; 힘들어요 = 'it is hard/I am exhausted'.
Often in 상황이 좋다/나쁘다 or 이런 상황에서 (in this situation).
Used as in 이리 오너라 (come here); 이리로 means 'this way'. Also can mean 'like this' (이렇게).

meaning: to seek, to look for (something needed)
note: Hanja 求; e.g. 직장을 구하다 (look for a job), 도움을 구하다 (seek help). Homonym of 구하다 'to rescue'.
Hanja 救; e.g. 생명을 구하다 (save a life). Homonym of 구하다 'to seek'.
Polite way to address a group, e.g. 학생 여러분 (students).
Pattern: 이상한 사람/소리 (strange person/sound); 이상해요 = 'it's strange'.
Takes an object: 추위를 느끼다 (feel cold), 행복을 느끼다 (feel happiness).

meaning: to fall, to drop; to fail; to run out
note: Several meanings: 비가 떨어지다 (fall), 시험에 떨어지다 (fail an exam), 돈이 떨어지다 (run out of money).
Can be intransitive or transitive: 차가 멈추다 (the car stops), 발걸음을 멈추다 (stop walking).

meaning: that kid, he/she (contraction of 그 아이)
note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이; 걔가 → 개가 is not used, say 걔가. Plural 걔네. Avoid in formal speech.
Verb form 준비하다 (to prepare); e.g. 시험 준비 (exam preparation).

meaning: to pass, to go by; to elapse
note: Used for places and time: 시간이 지나다 (time passes), 공원을 지나다 (pass a park).
Pattern: ~와/과 싸우다 (fight with ~); covers both physical fights and arguments.
Causative of 알다; pattern: ~에게 ~을 알리다 (notify someone of something).
Hanja 夫人; polite term for someone else's wife, e.g. 김 선생님 부인. Not used for one's own wife. Homonym 부인 (denial).
Common: 기억이 나다 (come to mind), 기억하다 (to remember). Before a vowel particle it links: 기억이 → 기어기.
Used for news, crimes and legal cases: 사건이 일어나다 (an incident occurs).
Can refer to people in general; also used for 'person' in a slightly negative tone (e.g. 나쁜 인간).

meaning: to take along (a person); to bring with one
note: Used only for people or animals, usually as 데리고 가다/오다. Use 가지고 for things.
Pattern: noun + 없이 (돈 없이 = without money).
Bound noun: verb stem + ㄴ/은 지 + time + 되다/지나다 (만난 지 오래되다). Written spaced from the verb.
Common: 걱정하다 (to worry), 걱정하지 마세요 (don't worry).

meaning: to be heard; to be audible
note: Passive of 듣다: 소리가 들리다. Different from 듣다 (to listen/hear actively).
Often as 잃어버리다 (to lose, e.g. a wallet). Distinct from 지다 (to lose a game).
Used with past tense: 방금 도착했어요.
Both intransitive (it moves) and transitive (to move something).
Pronounced as written; 이해 + 하다. 이해해요 = I understand.

meaning: to follow (someone behind); to follow (rules, advice)
note: Irregular (ㅡ-drop): 따라요, 따랐어요. Pattern: ~을/를 따라가다, ~에 따라.
Irregular (ㅡ-drop): 따라요, 따랐어요. Same spelling and conjugation as 'to follow'; context tells them apart.
Often 오래 걸리다 (take long), 오래되다 (be old/long-standing).
Honorific for another's 말, or humble for one's own words to elders: 말씀하세요, 말씀드리다.
Often 바라요 / ~기를 바라다 (I hope that...). Not 바래요 in standard spelling.
Can also act like an adjective with 의: 최고의 선수. 최고예요 = it's the best. Pronunciation is standard; 최 may be heard as [채/췌] only loosely.
Common phrase: 신경(을) 쓰다 (to care about/pay attention to).
Also a noun meaning 'fault/mistake' (제 잘못이에요). Before a vowel particle it links: 잘못이 → [잘모시]. Common: 잘못하다, 잘못 알다.

meaning: to be (located), to stay (honorific of 있다)
note: Honorific of 있다 for people one respects: 선생님은 집에 계세요. Do not use for yourself.
Pattern: 꿈을 꾸다 (to have a dream); also means a hope/goal.

meaning: guy, fellow; little rascal (casual, often affectionate or belittling)
note: Listed as a bound noun; used for a boy, child or animal, e.g. 이 녀석. Can sound rude about adults.

meaning: to be possible (synonym: 할 수 있다)
note: Pattern: N이/가 가능하다 (e.g. 사용이 가능하다). Opposite: 불가능하다.
Common pattern: 계획을 세우다 (to make a plan). ㅎ after ㄱ is not aspirated here since the ㅎ begins the next syllable's final; commonly [계훽/게훽].

meaning: to keep, protect, observe (a promise, rule)
note: Common: 약속을 지키다 (keep a promise), 규칙을 지키다, 지켜 주다.

meaning: to hit, strike, slap (e.g. the face)
note: 치다 has many meanings (play tennis/piano, type, etc.). Here: 얼굴을 치다 = to hit someone's face.
Common: 정신을 차리다 (come to one's senses), 정신이 없다 (be in a daze/busy).
Slightly more formal than 잠깐, e.g. 잠시만 기다려 주세요.
Common: 기회가 오다, 기회를 놓치다 (miss a chance).

meaning: to bring, take and come with (something)
note: Pattern: N을 가져오다. Opposite direction: 가져가다 (to take away).
Refers to a person's life journey; 삶 is more literary.
Before a vowel the ㄹ links: 삶이 [살미]. Derived from the verb 살다.
Common: 거짓말을 하다 (to tell a lie).

meaning: to spend time, get along, live (e.g. how one is doing)
note: Common: 잘 지내요? (How are you doing?), 친구와 잘 지내다.
Common: 힘이 세다 (be strong), 힘을 내다 (cheer up), 힘들다 (be hard).
With a negative it means 'hardly': 거의 없다. Without: 거의 다 (almost all).
Also used as a noun-like: 물론이다 (of course); 물론이에요. ㄹ+ㄹ both are pronounced as ㄹ.

meaning: to be careful, take care, watch out
note: Common: 조심하세요 (be careful), 감기 조심하세요. Pattern: N을/를 조심하다.

meaning: not at all, never (used with negatives)
note: Used with negative verbs: 전혀 모르다 (to not know at all). Often softened to [저녀] in fast speech.
옷을 걸다 = to hang clothes. Also means to make (a phone call: 전화를 걸다). ㄹ-irregular verb (거는, 겁니다).
물에 빠지다 = to fall into water. Also used figuratively: 사랑에 빠지다 (to fall in love).
머리가 빠지다 = hair falls out. Also means to be missing/omitted (이름이 빠졌다).

meaning: then, in that case; if so
note: Connects sentences. Often shortened to 그럼 in speech.
Used as 확인하다 or noun 확인 + 하다: 시간을 확인하다 (check the time).
Loanword from English. E.g. 팀장 (team leader), 같은 팀 (same team).
ㅂ-irregular (새로운, 새로워요). Often used for fresh/novel feelings; 새 is the determiner 'new' before a noun.
자리가 없다 = there is no seat/room. Also means position or occasion (자리에 앉다 to sit down).
Refers to a time already mentioned: 그때 나는 학생이었어요. Can be written 그 때 in older usage but 그때 is standard.
박사 학위 = doctorate degree. Also used for an expert/know-it-all (척척박사). Not a medical doctor (that is 의사).
Often 기억나다 = a memory comes to mind. Opposite is 잊다.

meaning: to be scary, frightening; to be afraid
note: ㅂ-irregular (무서운, 무서워요). 무서워하다 = to fear something.
Used for a duration of one day or a whole day (하루 종일 all day long). Also 'the first day of the month' in native counting.
피를 흘리다 = to bleed. 피가 나다 = to bleed (blood comes out).

meaning: well..., let me think; I'm not sure
note: Used when unsure or hesitant to answer: 글쎄요 (polite). Can also express disagreement or insistence.
Always before a noun: 첫날 (first day), 첫사랑 (first love), 첫눈 (first snow). Final ㅊ is pronounced [ㄷ]; 첫 + vowel links as 처시 but it is only used before nouns.

meaning: to get, to obtain, to gain
note: Used for abstract things you acquire: 정보를 얻다 (get information), 도움을 얻다. Not for receiving physical objects (받다).
Often 잊어버리다 (to forget completely). 잊어요 links as 이저요. Compare with 까먹다 (casual).
Used for children or young people; for people older than a child, 젊다 means 'to be young' (youthful).

meaning: to well up (of tears); to be reflected or hover (of a look or feeling)
note: Common pattern: 눈에 눈물이 어리다 (tears well up in the eyes). Different word from the adjective 어리다.
Often used to ask politely: 혹시 ~ 아세요? (Do you happen to know...?). Also used in 혹시(나) ~ㄹ까 봐 (in case).
Bound noun used after a noun or modifier: 오른쪽 (right side), 이쪽 (this way). Often written attached to the preceding word.
Used as a page counter after Sino-Korean numbers: 10쪽 (page 10). Also means 'side/face' of something, e.g. a page. Distinct from the direction sense.
Noun 안전 (safety); opposite is 위험하다. Adverb form: 안전하게.
Common pattern: 건강 상태 (health condition), 상태가 좋다/나쁘다.

meaning: to take (a person or animal) along
note: Used for people and animals only; for things use 가져가다. Opposite: 데려오다 (to bring along).
Noun 위험 (danger); opposite is 안전하다.
Often with honorific 부모님 (someone's parents, polite).
Often used as 나중에 (later). Opposite of 먼저 (first).

meaning: to be fun (casual, short for 재미있다)
note: Contraction of 재미있다, very common in speech. Pronounced as written ㅆ→ㄷ before ㄷ: 재믿따.
The physical organ; for the heart as feelings use 마음. Example: 심장이 뛰다 (heart beats).
Pairs with 질 (quality). Example: 양이 많다/적다 (the amount is large/small).
Pattern: A가 B를 이기다 / B에게 이기다. Opposite: 지다 (to lose).
Describes something no longer visible or existing; subject is usually the thing that disappears.
Also functions as a noun, e.g. 직접 만들다 (make it oneself). Opposite: 간접 (indirect).
Examples: 친구 사이 (relationship between friends), 두 건물 사이 (between two buildings).
English loanword; common patterns: 파티를 하다/열다 (to hold a party).

meaning: this way; this side (direction/location near the speaker)
note: Also used to mean 'this person' politely when introducing someone: 이쪽은 제 친구예요.
Also a rude word for a person (이 자식 = 'this bastard/guy'). For one's own children, 아이 or 아들/딸 are more neutral.
Can be teasing among friends but insulting otherwise.
Used to address or refer to a middle-aged man; can sound impolite to some. Female counterpart: 아줌마.
Native Korean number 셋 becomes 세 before counters: 세 권 (three volumes). 석/서 are used before some counters like 장 in older usage, but 세 is standard.

meaning: to be glad (to meet); to be pleased
note: Common phrase: 만나서 반갑습니다 (Nice to meet you).

meaning: to be certain; to be sure
note: Pattern: 확실히 (certainly, adverb); 확실하지 않다 = to be uncertain.
Also means 'as usual/so-so' (그저 그렇다 = so-so). Synonym of 단지 in the 'merely' sense.
Used for intense or random actions: 막 먹다, 막 울다.

meaning: just now; right (at the moment of)
note: Often with -(으)ㄹ 참이다 or -았/었어요: 막 도착했어요 (I just arrived); 막 -려고 하다 = about to.
Also a suffix-like noun for 'way of doing': 사용법 (how to use). Related: 법률 (law).
Common: 비밀을 지키다 (to keep a secret), 비밀번호 (password).
Contraction of 저것; with particles 저게 (subject), 저걸 (object).
Pattern: -는 순간 (the moment that...); 순간적 (momentary).
More formal/written than 여기. With a particle, ㅅ links: 이곳에서 → 이고세서.

meaning: to be ruined; to fail; to perish
note: Casually used for failure: 시험 망했어 (I bombed the test). Business: 가게가 망하다.
Related: 세계적 (worldwide), 세계 여행 (world travel).
Emphatic form of 정말; used to stress sincerity or degree.

meaning: properly; as it should be; correctly
note: Often with negatives: 제대로 못 하다 (can't do it properly).

meaning: as; according to; just as (bound noun)
note: Bound noun, written separately after a verb modifier: 말한 대로 (as I said), 아는 대로 (as far as I know). Attached without space after a noun as a particle: 법대로 (by the law).
Common pattern: 전쟁이 일어나다 (a war breaks out), 전쟁을 하다 (to wage war).
Mostly used in patterns like 상관없다 (it doesn't matter) and ~와/과 상관이 있다 (to be related to). Also means 'superior (officer)' in another sense.

meaning: to shoot, to fire; to sting
note: Also used for bee/insect stings (벌이 쏘다) and for 'to treat' in slang (한턱 쏘다).
Pattern: ~와/과 결혼하다 (to marry someone). Often softened to [겨로나다] in fast speech.

meaning: to promise; to make an appointment
note: Noun 약속 is also used: 약속이 있다 (have plans).

meaning: to save (a life), to revive; to make use of
note: Causative of 살다. Also means to bring out or make the most of something (장점을 살리다).
Neutral for animal young (강아지 새끼). Used about people it can be an insult or rough slang; avoid in polite speech.
Verb: 이해하다 (to understand); 이해가 되다/안 되다 (makes sense / doesn't).
Pattern: 정보를 얻다 (get information), 정보를 찾다 (look up information).
Casual speech often uses 완전 as an intensifier ('totally').
Noun form of 죽다.
Pattern: 소식을 듣다 (hear news), 소식을 전하다 (convey news). Usually about people's situations; 뉴스 is for media news.

meaning: to stamp; to take (a photo); to stab/dot
note: Here: 도장을 찍다 (to stamp a seal). Also 사진을 찍다 (take a photo).
Related: 여왕 (queen), 왕자 (prince). Also a slang prefix meaning 'huge/extreme'.
Common: 걱정하지 마세요 (don't worry). Noun 걱정 is also used: 걱정이 되다.
Sense of 바라진 모양 (being wide/just fitting): 딱 맞다 (fit perfectly). Also 딱 한 번 (just once).

meaning: to take charge of, to be in charge of; to smell
note: Here: 담임을 맡다 (to be the homeroom teacher). Also 냄새를 맡다 (smell something).

meaning: to suffer, to fall victim to; to be subjected to
note: Used for unpleasant things: 사기를 당하다 (be cheated), 무시를 당하다 (be disrespected).

meaning: honey; dear (term of address between spouses); hey (calling someone)
note: Used by married couples to address each other; also used as 'hello' on the phone in older speech.

meaning: to be excellent; to be great
note: Used to praise people, work or results. Pronounced as spelled; ㄹ+ㄹ in 륭 is already written, no change.

meaning: to pass on; to deliver (a message, news)
note: Common pattern: 안부를 전하다 (pass on regards), 소식을 전하다 (deliver news).
Used with 칼로 자르다 (cut with a knife).
Pattern: N 대신(에) 'instead of N'; V-는 대신 'in exchange for/instead of doing'.
Bound noun used after a modifier or noun: 이런 식으로 'in this way', 한국식 'Korean style'. Also means 'ceremony' (결혼식) as a different sense.
Example: 서로 도와요 'We help each other.'

meaning: to concern; to be about (used as ~에 관하여/관한)
note: Almost always used as N에 관해(서)/관한 N 'about N, regarding N'.
A bit more formal than 아주 or 너무 in speech; common in writing.
Derived from 확실하다 'to be certain'. The ㅅ after the ㄱ final is tensified; ㄹ moves forward to 씰 but the 히 is kept as is.
Pattern: N에 관심이 있다/없다 'be interested/not interested in N'.
Emphatic form of 아마; usually paired with guesses like -ㄹ 것이다 / -ㄹ지도 모르다.

meaning: to bring (a person or animal along)
note: Used for people/animals only (things use 가져오다). Opposite: 데려가다 'to take along'.
Often used with ~뿐이다 or ~(ㄴ/는) 것뿐이다 'it is only...'. Different from the noun 단지 'housing complex'.
Example: 중요한 부분 'the important part'. Opposite: 전체 'whole'.

meaning: to take (something) along; to take away
note: For things (people use 데려가다). Opposite: 가져오다 'to bring'.

meaning: to take out; to pull out; to remove
note: Example: 가시를 빼다 'pull out a thorn'. Also means 'subtract' and 'lose (weight)'.
Pattern: 사고가 나다 'an accident happens'; 교통사고 'traffic accident'. Different from 사고 'thought' (思考).
From 당연하다 'to be natural, obvious'. Used to say something is a matter of course.

meaning: to be perfect; to be flawless
note: The ㄱ final of 벽 merges with ㅎ to give [ㅋ].

meaning: to be great, to be remarkable (impressive)
note: Used to praise people or things: 대단하네요! Can also mean 'extreme/severe' (대단한 더위). Adverb form 대단히 is more formal.

meaning: to raise, to put up (make go up)
note: Causative of 오르다. Common patterns: 가격을 올리다 (raise prices), 사진을 올리다 (upload a photo), 결혼식을 올리다 (hold a wedding).

meaning: to run, to gallop (of a horse, vehicle)
note: In 말을 달리다 it means to ride a horse at speed (transitive). 달리다 also has other senses, such as 'to be attached/hang' (매달리다 type) and 'to be short of' (힘이 달리다), which are different meanings.
